Enabled by default.name: Translator API on Android
Enabled by default.summary: Exposes the Translator JavaScript Web API on Chrome for Android (including Chrome Custom Tabs). Web applications can translate text locally using on-device models without sending page text to cloud endpoints. The TranslatorAPIAllowed enterprise policy (https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/translator-api-allowed/) is supported on Android to disable the API and prevent model downloads.
Enabled by default.creator: jaeone@google.com

Deprecated.name: More specific protocol filtering in Digital Credential API
Deprecated.summary:
Chrome 151 began deprecating support for unspecified presentation and issuance protocols in the **Digital Credentials API**. Final removal of support is now scheduled for Chrome 161.

The Digital Credentials API was originally designed to be an opaque pipeline for arbitrary exchange protocols. In November 2025, the [FedID WG resolved](https://github.com/w3c-fedid/digital-credentials/issues/396) to change this so that the spec normatively referenced only a specific set of exchange protocols.

The removal of support for arbitrary, opaque pipelines ensures that only verified protocols are used, enabling a more robust privacy and security threat model for identity verification. This change aligns Chromium with the updated industry specification.
Deprecated.creator: rbyers@chromium.org

view.notes: Mozilla is officially negative on the DC API itself. In the FedID WG meeting for restricting the API to specified protocols only, Mozilla representatives argued in favor of the change.
Supports only the org-iso-mdoc protocol already
